title: Still
description: One Mode B close-up: a high-resolution still with its camera pose and the targets the backend asked for. camera is in arkit_world (metres, Y up) from the phone; the backend adds camera_design in the design frame (model.glb: millimetres, Z up) after alignment and per-still re-registration. The backend projects each target into the still from camera_design and the target's design-frame box.

scan_id.description: The Mode A scan this still is registered to.

kind.description: guided: AR-ring target with pose. macro_detail: ultrawide macro outside the AR session, no reliable pose, evidence-only. label: product label for identification. unguided: a still taken without a target ring, e.g. a frame of an imported capture (B12) or a plain camera photo (tools/import_photos.py, pose_reliable false, no camera); targets is empty.

image_file.description: JPEG (q >= 85). HEIC is converted on the phone; Grain does not accept it.

camera.description: Camera pose in arkit_world at capture (from the ARFrame returned with the still). For macro_detail this is the last AR pose and is approximate. May be absent only when pose_reliable is false: a plain photo has no pose, and none is made up.

camera_design.description: Backend-filled pose in the design frame (mm, Z up) after alignment and depth re-registration.

pose_reliable.description: False for macro_detail, when tracking was limited, or when the still has no pose at all (a plain photo: camera absent). Only when false may camera and intrinsics be absent.

intrinsics.description: Pinhole intrinsics in pixels of the width_px x height_px image. May be absent only when pose_reliable is false and the focal length is unknown (a plain photo without EXIF focal length).

depth_file.description: Nearest ARKit depth frame (256x192) for re-registration.

targets.description: What the backend asked this still to cover. Empty for a label still.

part_refs.description: Grain part names (model.glb nodes, diagnose parts[].name) expected in view, e.g. J1, LOAD1.

harness_rows.description: harness.csv wire names expected in view, e.g. WIRE_A.

box_mm.description: The target's box in the design frame (mm, Z up), from the model.glb node bounds. Connector-level, because Grain has no pin positions yet (G25; pins are target T7).

attached_to_target_id.description: For macro_detail: the guided target this detail belongs to.

tracking_state.description: unknown: the capture app did not record it (an import); pose_reliable is then absent, or false when there is no pose at all (a plain photo).

auto_fired.description: True when the app took the shot because the ring filled, tracking was normal and sharpness was high.

user_skipped.description: True when the user tapped 'skip, I can't reach it'. Targets then become not_inspected.

segment.description: Capture segment (absent = 0). The app starts segment 1 after the person flips the object for the underside: the object moved, so poses from different segments are not in the same object frame. Stills of segment ≥ 1 are pose_reliable false until the segments are registered (on the Mac); their camera pose stays in the session's world frame.

exposure_s.description: Exposure duration of the still (ARKit camera).

iso.description: ISO of the still, from the frame's EXIF when ARKit gives it.

depth_gap_ms.description: Time between the still and the regular ARKit frame its depth_file came from (high-res frames carry no depth).

torch_level.description: Torch level during the still (0 = off); torch_on is level > 0.

view_cell.description: The coverage-dome cell the still was taken from (app scan, e.g. r1s05: elevation ring 0-2 above the support plane, azimuth sector 0-11 around the object; in a hand-held scan, pose_source object_tracked, b1s05 is a view of the underside, ring 1-2 below the object's middle, in the object frame). Lets the backend see which sides were photographed.

pose_source.description: Where camera comes from. arkit (also when absent): ARKit world tracking. object_tracked: the app's hand-held mode: the camera relative to the tracked, moving object, in the scan's object frame (the ARKit world frame at the moment the object was locked; see scan-package pose_source).

pose_quality.description: The object tracker's confidence in camera, 0-1 (object_tracked only). Below 0.55 the app marks pose_reliable false; below 0.7 locate caps its confidence at medium.

low_light.description: True when the app took the still in low light (it never blocks on light): judge dark detail with care.

pose_arkit.description: Camera-to-world pose in ARKit's world frame: metres, Y up. Camera axes as ARKit (x right, y up, looking along -z).

pose_design.description: Camera-to-design pose in the design frame (model.glb): millimetres, Z up. Same camera axes as pose_arkit.
